properties.name: Every release says what it brings to the VS Code --call setup, and what still needs flo2.io's gateway
properties.statement: Every reflow2 release, on an ongoing basis, says in its release notes what it adds to the VS Code --call setup (a one-shot call on the design on your own machine, used where MCP is blocked, as at Anthony's work) and which of its changes still need flo2.io's gateway rather than --call. Anthony's words, 2026-10-12, given as the model for every release: "0.83.2 binary isn't out yet, but once released it'll add reply budgets and paging support to your VS Code --call setup, though hub-view features (merged search, cross-design reads) will still require flo2.io's gateway rather than --call." The point is that a person who works through --call can tell, from the release alone, what they can use there and what they cannot, without asking. Each statement is checked against the released binary through --call, not inferred from the code. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
